1.2
Aleksandra Savic - Cost of Pool Rental for Burnaby Water Polo Club
1.
Aleksandra Savic - Cost of Pool Rental for Burnaby Water Polo Club.pdf
Copy: Chief Administrative Officer, General Manager Corporate Services, General Manager Parks, Recreation and Culture
Note from General Manager Parks, Recreation and
Culture
: Burnaby Water Polo Club has raised concerns about pool rental costs, facility availability, and youth participation impacts. Due to the nature of the sport, the club requires full-pool rentals, often outside regular operating hours, resulting in additional staffing costs and higher rental fees compared to groups that can accommodate more participants through lane rentals. Staff will continue to work with the club to review its pool time requirements and identify opportunities to optimize bookings and minimize rental costs.
1.3
Alex Goldkind - High-Speed Electric Bikes and Scooters on Shared Pathways
1.
Alex Goldkind - High-Speed Electric Bikes and Scooters on Shared Pathways.pdf
Copy: Chief Administrative Officer, General Manager Corporate Services, General Manager Engineering, Acting General Manager Community Safety
Note from General Manager Engineering:
The motor sizes and speed thresholds for e-bikes and e-scooters are regulated under B.C.’s
Motor Vehicle Act
.  Burnaby RCMP maintains jurisdiction over the enforcement of these provisions and violations, which are subject to statutory fines set by the Province.  Staff continue to work with the Province and RCMP to address e-bike and e-scooter safety and coordinate enforcement.  Further public guidance on usage is shared on the City website.
1.4
Liliana Tosic - Traffic Calming Measures at Alderwood Crescent
1.
Liliana Tosic - Traffic Calming Measures at Alderwood Crescent.pdf
Copy: Chief Administrative Officer, General Manager Corporate Services, General Manager Community Safety, General Manager Engineering
Note from General Manager Engineering:
Staff have completed the technical review on Alderwood Crescent, and no speed management measures are warranted at this time. The requested warning signs do not align with engineering design guidelines, which support the consistent and uniform application of traffic control devices throughout the road network to meet driver expectations. Staff will correspond directly with the inquirer regarding the recently raised concern about visibility at the west-side blind corner.
1.5
Maria Melo - Mainline Sewer Capacity Issue on the 4500 Block of Frances Street
1.
Maria Melo - Mainline Sewer Capacity Issue on the 4500 Block of Frances Street.pdf

Note from General Manager Engineering:
Engineering staff have been working directly with the property owner and have undertaken several operational and investigative measures to help mitigate the risk and identify potential contributing factors. Staff will continue to monitor sewer system performance and review available information to better understand the cause of the localized flooding and determine whether any further action is required. Engineering will continue working with the property owner as the investigation progresses.

While motorcycles have a smaller road footprint, they can play a meaningful role in reducing traffic congestion and lowering emissions.  Staff recognize the value of supporting various travel modes and will review opportunities to integrate motorcycles into our future parking policy and curbside use, where feasible.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider laneway home construction concerns in Burnaby's R1 district
agenda_briefs.summary: Ainsley Clement of Portland Street Laneway Homes has filed a formal complaint with Burnaby Council about laneway homes in South Burnaby, saying the situation is "out of control" and harming privacy, safety and neighbourhood character, with insufficient parking and infrastructure to support the added housing. Planning and Development staff say they will contact the writer directly. No rule changes have been proposed; any would need their own approval process.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for any follow-up from Burnaby Planning and Development if you build or plan laneway homes in the R1 district.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to review Burnaby Water Polo Club pool rental costs and booking options
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to look at a report on pool rental costs for the Burnaby Water Polo Club. The club has raised concerns about how much it pays to rent city pools, how often facilities are available, and how these costs affect youth participation. Because the sport needs the whole pool — often outside normal hours — the club pays more for extra staff than groups that share lanes. City staff say they will keep working with the club to review its pool time needs and find ways to improve bookings and lower rental costs. No decision has been made yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If you run a group that rents Burnaby pools, watch for the council decision and ask staff about booking options that could lower your costs.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider e-bike and e-scooter safety on Burnaby shared pathways
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider a report on high-speed electric bikes and e-scooters on shared pathways. City staff note that motor sizes and speed limits for these devices are set by B.C.'s Motor Vehicle Act, and that the Burnaby RCMP — not the City — enforces those rules, with fines set by the Province. Staff say they will keep working with the Province and RCMP on safety and enforcement, and that public guidance is posted on the City website. No new City rule has been approved yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision and check the City website for e-bike and e-scooter usage guidance if your business relies on shared pathways.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider staff finding that no traffic calming is needed on Alderwood Crescent
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will consider a staff report on a resident's request for traffic calming measures on Alderwood Crescent. Engineering staff completed a technical review and concluded that no speed management measures are warranted at this time. Staff also say the requested warning signs do not fit provincial engineering design guidelines, which call for traffic signs to be applied the same way across the road network so drivers know what to expect. Staff will write directly to the resident about a separate concern raised about visibility at the blind corner on the west side. No bylaw changes are proposed.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider sewer capacity investigation on 4500 block Frances Street
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider a report on sewer capacity problems on the 4500 block of Frances Street, where localized flooding has been reported. Engineering staff say they have been working directly with the property owner and have taken several operational and investigative steps to reduce the risk and find possible causes. Staff will keep monitoring how the sewer system performs and review information to better understand the flooding and decide whether more action is needed. The investigation is ongoing and no decision has been made yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If your property is near the 4500 block of Frances Street, report any sewer backups or flooding to Engineering and keep records of damage.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider request to fold part of North Howard Avenue into Capitol Hill Conservation Area
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will consider a request from Robert Anderson to make part of North Howard Avenue part of the Capitol Hill Conservation Area. Staff say fully dealing with the request would mean looking at closing roads and rezoning and/or combining several parcels of land. Rezoning means changing the official rules for how land can be used. Staff will review the proposal, respond to Mr. Anderson, and figure out the best way to handle it. No decision has been made yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the staff response and any rezoning or road-closure reports if you own property near North Howard Avenue or the Capitol Hill Conservation Area.

This is a report note, not a final council decision.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider referring North Burnaby driving and cycling safety concerns to Transportation Committee
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider referring resident Ed Pereira's five North Burnaby driving and cycling safety concerns to the Transportation Committee. The letter asks the City to keep Douglas Road open at Lougheed Highway so Delta Avenue traffic can connect to the planned Dawson Street connector, add reflectors at the Willingdon-Dawson intersection, install blind-spot warning signs and speed measures on Gilmore at Halifax/1st Avenue, add bicycle bypass gaps to all speed bumps (including 13 humps on the Union Street bike route from Duthie to Kensington), and make curb ramps standard citywide. No road changes have been approved.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on this referral — no action is needed unless you want to raise your own road safety concerns with the City.

agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a request from the Village of Pouce Coupe asking the province to bring back the Rural Homeowners Benefit. That benefit was a provincial grant that reduced property taxes for homeowners in rural areas. The request comes as a letter from Pouce Coupe, and Council has not yet voted on whether to support it. If Council backs the request, it would only be Burnaby's endorsement — the province would still decide whether to reinstate the benefit.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Hastings Street signal timing and spillover traffic concerns
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a resident's request to review the cumulative effect of pedestrian-controlled signals along Hastings Street, which he says cause frequent stops and push drivers onto residential streets like Curtis and Parker. He asks Council to direct staff to consider signal timing, coordination, or alternative crossing designs. The agenda item includes no proposed bylaw or staff recommendation, so it is unclear what Council may decide. Copies went to the Chief Administrative Officer and the General Managers of Corporate Services and Engineering.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision — any changes to Hastings Street signal timing or traffic rules could affect access to your business.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider signal changes at Kensington Avenue and Joe Sakic Way
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a resident's request that Engineering review signal coordination, vehicle detection, pedestrian call timing and actual delays at Kensington Avenue at the Christine Sinclair Community Centre and Joe Sakic Way. Alex Goldkind reports that about 98% of his trips through the section are stopped at one or both signals, and asks Council to direct a review, explain feasible changes and timelines, and provide a substantive written reply rather than another referral to Engineering. No decision has been made.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch the council meeting outcome if your business depends on traffic flow or access at Kensington Avenue and Joe Sakic Way.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider correspondence on Hart House and increased housing density
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a piece of correspondence from Andre Bidaud about Hart House and increased housing density. The item appears on the agenda as a referral, meaning Council may simply receive the letter and send copies to senior staff — the Chief Administrative Officer, the General Manager of Corporate Services, the Deputy CAO/General Manager of Lands and Facilities, the General Manager of Planning and Development, and the Director of Intergovernmental Relations and Public Affairs. No bylaw, rezoning, or policy change is up for a vote at this stage. If Council later moves toward more density near Hart House, new rules for development in that area could follow in a future report or public hearing.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch the meeting outcome — if Council asks staff to study more density near Hart House, expect future zoning or development changes in that area.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider resident letters on Bill 44 and SSMUH housing rules
agenda_briefs.summary: Three Burnaby residents have written to Council asking it to pause approvals of new multiplex developments and any further bylaw changes that expand them, until the incoming provincial government clarifies what will happen to Bill 44. The letters cite the Premier-elect's stated intent to give municipalities more control over neighbourhood density, and ask Council to consult residents, including through public hearings, before any further zoning changes. No vote or change to the rules is described in this item.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for any Council direction on pausing Bill 44 multiplex approvals that could affect what you can build or redevelop on your property.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider annual Diwali fireworks exemption request in Burnaby
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a request from Ramana Saranam to amend the Fire Services Bylaw to allow low-hazard fireworks on Diwali each year, mirroring the existing October 31 allowance. Currently, low-hazard fireworks are only permitted on October 31 for people 18 and older on private property with owner consent; other dates require a Fire Chief special-occasion permit. The sale of fireworks in Burnaby is prohibited, and fireworks cannot be discharged on public property without a Fire Chief permit. The Fire Chief says only Council can create an annual exemption.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Note that selling fireworks in Burnaby remains prohibited and any Diwali exemption would require a Council bylaw amendment, not a Fire Department decision.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider residential parking restrictions on Pandora Street
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a request from Syed Zaidi about residential parking restrictions on Pandora Street. The item appears on the meeting agenda, and copies have been sent to the Chief Administrative Officer and senior staff in Corporate Services and Engineering. The agenda does not say what specific parking rules are being asked for, such as permit-only zones, time limits, or changes to who can park on the street. No decision has been made yet. If Council moves the item forward, staff may be asked to review the request and report back before any parking bylaw change is voted on.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch the council meeting outcome and any staff report on Pandora Street parking, since new restrictions could affect customer and staff parking.
